biteOfDay: ing Stocked rainbows on Taneycomo continue to feed aggressively in the seams during low-water windows, with more browns beginning to show as we move deeper into the early-fall window. On Table Rock, bass are sliding off summer shallows toward points, creek channels, and deeper structure in the clear water.

tableRock.clarity: Clear near dam (typical); verify arms locally

taneycomo.temp: Tailwater cold (typically ~50–54°F). Verify at the bank.
taneycomo.generation: ~20 cfs at 12:00 CT (USACE live). Overnight ~20; afternoon peak ~20. Call SWPA 866-494-1993 before you wad.

species.name: Bass
species.technique: Topwater at dawn; deep spoon, shakey head, deep crank mid-day

species.name: Walleye
species.technique: Crankbaits, live bait (carried mid-summer pattern — not freshly guide-verified 07-21)

species.name: Crappie
species.depth: Deep timber & brush piles (James River/Long Creek arms)
species.technique: Small white or yellow jigs under deep-water docks

species.name: Trout
species.technique: Low-flow morning window; pink worms/jigs/midges; drift when generation heavy (Trophy Area nightcrawlers)

species.name: Bluegill
species.technique: Worms, small poppers — great for kids (mid-summer pattern carry)

species.name: Catfish
species.depth: Indian Point & near dam, shallows after dark
species.technique: Stink bait, hot dogs, cut/frozen bait — evening/night

tip: Insider tip: Take advantage of the typical low morning flows on Taneycomo. Wade or drift seams and current breaks with a 1/16- to 1/8-oz micro jig (brown, black, white or sculpin) or a zebra midge under an indicator. When the generators come online later, switch to heavier rigs and target the breaks
